data.name: Nicodemius
data.gender_notes: Nicodemius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew 'Nikodemus', meaning 'victory of the people', this name has deep roots in both biblical and saintly tradition. In the New Testament, Nicodemus is mentioned as a Pharisee who secretly became a disciple of Jesus. In the Acts of the Apostles, he is recorded as being present during the crucifixion and burial of Jesus, and later as one of the seventy disciples sent out to spread the gospel. Through his courage and faith, Nicodemus became a powerful symbol of the transformative power of the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of transformation and courage in the face of adversity
data.etymology: Nicodemius belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nicodemius total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: ניקודמוס
in_hebrew.meaning: ניקודמוס: כובש עם הניקוד, מנצח עם הניקוד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ניקודמוס הוא שם המורכב מיוונית עתיקה, ניקו (נίκη) - ניצחון, ודמוס (δῆμος) - עם, עמי. הוא מתורגם כובש עם הניקוד או מנצח עם הניקוד. השם ניקודמוס מוזכר בברית החדשה, בבשורה על-פי יוחנן, כאדם שהיה פאראיסאי ורופא, אשר בא לישוע בלילה כדי ללמוד ממנו.

in_greek.name: Νικόδημος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νικόδημος είναι όνομα ελληνικής προέλευσης, αποτελούμενο από το νίκη (nίκη) που σημαίνει 'νίκη' και το δῆμος (dēmos) που σημαίνει 'λαός' ή 'πληθυσμός'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, συγκεκριμένα στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ιωάννη, ο Νικόδημος αναφέρεται ως Φαρισαίος και γιατρός, που ήρθε στον Ιησού τη νύχτα για να μάθει από Εκείνον.

in_latin.name: Nicodemius
in_latin.long_meaning: Nicodemius nomen est origine Graeca, compositum ex victoria (nike) et populo (demos). Significat victorem populi vel triumphatorem plebis. In Novo Testaments, nomine Nicodemus, homo Pharisaeus et medicus, noctu ad Iesum venit ut ab eo disceret.

in_english.name: Nicodemius
in_english.meaning: Nicodemius: victorious among the people, conqueror of the masses
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nicodemius originates from Greek roots, 'nike' (victory) and 'demos' (people). It signifies one who is victorious among the people or a conqueror of the masses. Nicodemus, as referenced in the New Testament, specifically in the Gospel of John, was a Pharisee and a doctor who came to Jesus at night to learn from Him. The name has been used in Christian tradition to symbolize spiritual victory and enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nicodemus has historical ties to the Jewish background of early Christianity, and its mention in the New Testament has made it a name with rich cultural impact. It is often referenced in discussions of Christian history and doctrine, particularly in regards to the Jewish-Christian connections and the role of Pharisees in the spread of Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: The cultural resonance of the name Nicodemus is closely tied to its spiritual significance. This name represents the transformative power of the Christian faith through the example of its bearer. Nicodemus' secret conversion from a Pharisee to a disciple of Jesus is a powerful reminder of the journey of faith and the courage required to embrace the teachings of Jesus, even in the face of opposition.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicodemus: From the Greek, meaning "victory of the people of God." A Pharisee and secret disciple of Jesus, embodying the struggle between adherence to religious tradition and the call for spiritual renewal through Christ.

biblical_reference.note: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a secret follower of Jesus.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Nicodemus was a Jewish leader who secretly helped Jesus and his disciples. The name Nicodemius carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Nicodemius, a minister in London, United Kingdom, shares that their name Nicodemius meaning "Victory of the people" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
